summary.headline: Bharat Parenterals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 110% YoY to INR136.3 crores and the group swung to a INR11.8 crore profit after tax.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR136.3 crores (up 110% YoY, up 45% QoQ) with EBITDA of INR26.6 crores at a 17.3% margin, versus INR8.5 crores at 9.1% in Q1. Innoxel Life Sciences drove the improvement, with revenue of INR44.5 crores at a 33% EBITDA margin, while standalone revenue of INR78.6 crores was held back by a sharp input-cost-driven gross margin fall to 35%. Management maintained FY27 guidance for standalone and Varenyam Healthcare, and kept Innoxel's margin guidance under review until Q3. A preferential issue of about INR139 crores was approved, with the proceeds not yet in the 30 September balance sheet.

segments.name: Standalone (BPL)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR78.6 crores, with EBITDA INR7 crores at 9% margin, down from 12.3% in Q1, as input material costs rose about 5 percentage points of revenue. Domestic tender book fell from INR119 crores (June) to INR65 crores (September); total order book INR117 crores. Q2 included about INR25-30 crores of deferred export tender supply.

segments.name: Innoxel Life Sciences (55.9% owned)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR44.5 crores at 33% EBITDA margin, mostly licensing, milestone and development income. First CMO product (oral liquid) exported to the US on 20 October, after quarter end, with no revenue yet in Q2. Management maintains FY27 guidance of 35-40% revenue growth and 20-25% margin, excluding licensing income of INR80-90 crores.

segments.name: Varenyam Healthcare (domestic branded)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR19.7 crores (up 33.2% YoY), EBITDA margin 9.2%. H1 revenue INR44.9 crores (up 43.2%) at 11% margin. FY27 guidance is 20-25% growth and 8-13% margin; 229 field representatives against a year-end target of 250. Bhuvah women's health division launches later this year as a cost before revenue.

segments.name: Varenyam Biolifesciences (VBPL)
segments.commentary: Pre-revenue; Q2 operating cost INR0.14 crores and capital work in progress INR33.7 crores. Construction completion targeted for Q2 CY2028. Pivoted towards biologics CDMO with a 2,000 kL tank in phase 1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained. Standalone: revenue growth 10-15% on FY26 base of INR234 crores; EBITDA margin 10-15%.

Innoxel: revenue growth 35-45% and EBITDA margin 20-25%, excluding licensing income of INR80-90 crores. H1 is well ahead on revenue but just under the band on margin; revisions, if any, to be given after Q3.
Innoxel targets 10-12 signed out-licensing contracts by end-Q3 FY27 (six signed in H1), against a target of 12-15 a year.
Varenyam Healthcare: 20-25% growth and 8-13% margin retained; business tapers into Q4 and the new division is a cost.
No further equity dilution expected; capex to be funded internally plus bank debt at Varenyam Biolifesciences. Up to INR135 crores of the preferential issue goes to subsidiaries over two years.
EU GMP inspection expected in FY27, with no confirmed date from the regulator.
capex_capacity: Standalone general block utilisation 70% in H1 FY27 vs 48.5% in FY26; beta-lactam 33% (vs 21%); cephalosporins 31.5% (vs 24%). Management says no new capacity is needed for standalone guidance.
Standalone H1 capex about INR15 crores against INR65 crores cash from operations.
Liposomal skid in the general block: exhibit batches planned for November; filing targeted for Q1 of next financial year.
Innoxel holds a US FDA EIR and a Belgian GMP certificate covering all four lines.
VBPL: Phase 1 capex about INR300 crores, with one 2,000 kL tank; construction completion targeted for Q2 CY2028 subject to commissioning and regulatory timelines; phase 2 scope not yet defined.
demand_pricing: Standalone order book INR117 crores at end-September across domestic tenders, exports and international tenders. Management says the book was priced before input cost increases, so margins will stay under pressure until prices ease or the book turns over.

Management is shifting standalone growth towards branded business via new registrations, dossier filings and EU GMP/PIC/S approvals; tender business is being fulfilled but not expanded. Tender share was about 52% of revenue per an analyst citation; management did not confirm the split.
Innoxel: 48 projects across 18-19 clients under CDMO and CMO banners. Upfront payments are 10% or less of Innoxel revenue; the rest is milestone-based.
Innoxel 505(b)(2) products expected to achieve 10-15% market conversion in the first couple of years, per partner views; management cited 70-80% gross margins typical for these contracts.
Innoxel profit-share economics for own CDMO products expected from Q3 FY28 (505(b)(2)); management said margins could exceed 35-40% once profit-share income starts, with no firm number.

qa_highlights.question: How much of standalone Q2 revenue came from the deferred export tender?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR25-30 crores in Q2, with part of the total also recognised in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Given H1 Innoxel revenue of about INR65 crores, why keep FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth on a INR72 crore base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said licensing and milestone income is lumpy; it will review Innoxel guidance after Q3 and currently expects to meet the guided numbers, keeping the 20-25% margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR139 crore preferential issue fund Varenyam Biolifesciences or Innoxel?
qa_highlights.answer: It is earmarked for all subsidiaries as requirements arise; no split was given. A monitoring agency has been appointed.

qa_highlights.question: Could Innoxel cross INR300 crores of revenue in FY29, and what margin profile applies at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to INR300 crores and will update in FY28. Margins should rise once profit share from own products starts, possibly above 35-40%, but no firm number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will further dilution be needed to fund VBPL and Innoxel?
qa_highlights.answer: No further dilution is expected; capex will be funded from Innoxel and standalone cash flow plus the INR139 crore raise, with bank debt at VBPL.

qa_highlights.question: Can Innoxel's complex products be launched in India through Varenyam?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate plans; Indian pricing does not support the product costs from Innoxel.

risks_watch: Standalone margin: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 9% on input cost inflation (material cost up about 5 percentage points of revenue); the order book of INR117 crores was priced before the cost increase, so pressure persists until prices ease or the book turns over.

Innoxel revenue lumpiness: H1 revenue of INR65.9 crores is mostly milestone and licensing income, and management will revisit FY27 Innoxel growth and margin guidance only after Q3; watch the count of signed out-licensing contracts (six in H1, target 10-12 by end-Q3).

Standalone tender exposure and H2 growth: H1 standalone revenue was flat YoY, the domestic tender book fell from INR119 crores to INR65 crores, and Q2 included about INR25-30 crores of deferred export tender supply that will not recur at the same scale.
EU GMP inspection: management expects it in FY27 but has no confirmed regulator date; outcome and timing are open.

Commercial ramp and approvals: first CMO oral liquid product exported on 20 October with no revenue in Q2, binding forecast from partner awaited; liposomal exhibit batches planned for November with filing targeted for Q1 of next financial year.

Funding and capex: INR139 crore preferential issue (up to INR135 crores to subsidiaries over two years, no split between VBPL and Innoxel); VBPL phase 1 capex about INR300 crores with only INR33.7 crores CWIP so far, and construction completion targeted for Q2 CY2028; consolidated borrowings INR160 crores, and management says H1 working capital release of INR48.4 crores will not repeat at that scale.
key_quotes: Q2 is the first quarter where that inflection shows up in the group's profit.
Our material cost went up by about 5 percentage points of revenue in a single quarter and the gross margin came down to 35%
I will wait for Q3 before I give any if at all there is any guidance revision on Innoxel numbers because we have to see what kind of licensing and milestones can be achieved in H2.
We expect no further dilution at this moment in time.
No. We expect no further dilution at this moment in time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the consolidated turnaround, Innoxel's operating leverage and the FY27 standalone and Varenyam guidance, but explicitly cautious on standalone margins under input cost pressure and on Innoxel's lumpy milestone revenue, where it declined to revise guidance before Q3. It was evasive on several specifics, including the Innoxel FY29 INR300 crore question, the VBPL phase 2 scope, the Innoxel out-licensing split by subsidiary, and the Innoxel CMO forecast, saying it would answer in later quarters.

growth.why: FY27 guidance held: standalone revenue growth 10-15% on INR234 crore base, Innoxel 35-45% (ex-licensing INR80-90 crore), Varenyam 20-25%; backed by a INR117 crore standalone order book and Innoxel's 6 signed out-licensing deals in H1, but standalone margins are pressured by pre-increase pricing and no new standalone capacity is needed, while the main new capacity (VBPL, INR300 crore) is not live u

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 17.3% in Q2 from 9.1% in Q1, but standalone margin fell to 9% (from 12.3%) as input costs rose about 5 points of revenue and the INR117 crore order book was priced before the increase, so gains depend on Innoxel's lumpy licensing and on input prices easing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: VBPL phase 1 (2,000 kL tank, about INR300 crore capex) is under construction with only INR33.7 crore CWIP so far and completion targeted for Q2 CY2028, which is outside the 2-4 quarter window; standalone utilisation at 70% needs no new capacity per management.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 guidance held for standalone revenue growth of 10-15% on INR234 crore base and Innoxel 35-45%, backed by INR117 crore standalone order book and six signed out-licensing deals in H1, though H1 standalone revenue was flat YoY and the domestic tender book fell from INR119 crore to INR65 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone general block utilisation is 70% (beta-lactam 33%, cephalosporins 31.5%) with no new capacity needed for guidance, and the liposomal skid is only a minor add; a new capex announcement is conditional on Innoxel scaling and the Varenyam Bio phase 2 scope, which is not yet defined.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all FY27 guidance and will revisit Innoxel's 35-45% growth and 20-25% margin only after Q3, with Innoxel H1 margin just under the 20-25% band and standalone margin at 9% in Q2 against a 10-15% guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone Q2 EBITDA margin of 9% sits below the 10-15% FY27 guide, Innoxel H1 margin of 14% is below the 20-25% band, and Innoxel licensing income of INR80-90 crore depends on out-licensing contracts (six of 10-12 targeted by end-Q3).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY28 filing; Q3 FY27 exports
rows.why: Liposomal skid exhibit batches planned for November with filing targeted Q1 of next FY, and the first Innoxel CMO oral liquid was exported to the US on 20 October; Bhuvah women's health division launches later this year, and 505(b)(2) profit share starts Q3 FY28.

rows.label: Innoxel out-licensing contracts
rows.why: Six contracts signed in H1 against a target of 10-12 by end-Q3 and 12-15 for the year, so the pace needs to roughly double in H2 to hit targets.

rows.label: EU GMP inspection for standalone
rows.why: Management expects the inspection in FY27 but the regulator has not confirmed a date, and the outcome would unlock the EU/PIC/S branded push.

rows.label: Standalone input cost relief
rows.why: Gross margin fell to 35% from 44.1% a year ago and the order book was priced before input cost increases, so margin recovery needs prices to ease or the book to turn over.

tone.note: Management was confident on the consolidated turnaround, Innoxel operating leverage and the held FY27 guidance, but cautious on standalone margins under input cost pressure and on Innoxel's lumpy milestone revenue, and evasive on the INR300 crore FY29 question, VBPL phase 2 scope and the Innoxel CMO
